1.  The present application has been filed by the applicant seeking regular bail in FIR No. 626/2022 under Sections 376/377/506/354D of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Patel Nagar, Delhi.
2. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

3. Counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of the Court to the statements of the prosecutrix as well as the statement of the brother of the prosecutrix to submit that the applicant was in a consensual physical relationship with the prosecutrix.
This is a digitally signed order.

It is submitted that the FIR, dated 1st November 2022 has been filed in a highly belated manner.
5. Learned APP opposes the bail and submits that the testimony of the mother of the prosecutrix is yet to be recorded.
6. I have heard the counsels for the parties and perused the material on record.
7. In the present case, it cannot be denied that the prosecutrix had known the applicant and was meeting the applicant on a regular basis.
The evidence on record also suggests that the prosecutrix was in a relationship with another person during the same period.
Whether the consent of the prosecutrix was vitiated by the misconception of fact arising out of the promise to marry, cannot be established at this stage and would be a matter of trial.
8. In the present case, the FIR was registered on 1st November, 2022 even though the last sexual encounter between the applicant and prosecutrix was on 16th August, 2022.
9. The investigation in the present case is complete and the chargesheet has already been filed.
The statements of the material witnesses, the prosecutrix and her brother have been recorded.
10. The applicant has been in judicial custody since 1st November, 2022.

11. Considering the totality of aforesaid facts and circumstances and taking into account that the trial is likely to take some time, the applicant cannot be kept under incarceration for an indefinite period of time.
Therefore, this Court considers it fit to grant bail to the applicant.
12. For the forgoing reasons, the application is allowed and the applicant is directed to be released on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
This is a digitally signed order.

i.
The applicant shall not communicate with or come in contact with the prosecutrix or any of the prosecution witnesses or tamper with the evidence of the case.
ii. The applicant shall not leave the country without the prior permission of the Court.

iv. The applicant shall provide his latest/fresh mobile number(s) to the IO concerned,
which shall be kept in working condition at all times and shall not switch it off or change the mobile number(s) without prior intimation to the IO concerned.
v.

The applicant shall intimate the Court by way of an affidavit and to the IO regarding any change in his residential address.
13.

14. Accordingly, the application is disposed of.
